summary: Business With Brian's September 21 video argues AI spending cannot stop despite slowdown headlines, because the constraint is physical: fewer than 4% of US data centers can take a full rack of Nvidia's newest chips, grid connections take ~4 years, and hyperscalers hold ~$1.7T in signed backlog (~3 years of buildout at the 2026 pace). His framework: own the parts no AI lab can win without — memory, optics, inference — scored by his signal system. Memory: Micron (MU BUY, 'buy a little') — 80% operating margins on the shortage, but historically expensive, so he waits for the September 30 report before buying more; Sandisk (SNDK BUY) — 78% operating margins, under 8x forward earnings, 0.3 PEG, capped at 'buy' with only 19 months of history. Optics: Lumentum (LITE SELL — sell some; 195x trailing profit vs ~70x normal, price ran ahead despite 83% sales growth); Marvell (MRVL SELL — strongest sell signal; 80x vs 33x normal, Google's 6.7% stake deal already prices in 7 years of growth). Inference: Cerebras (CBRS CONDITIONAL BUY — $25B backlog vs <$1B sales, $8.6B cash; watch backlog conversion) and CoreWeave (CRWV UNCERTAIN — burned $13.7B cash in 12 months on $7.6B sales). Nvidia (NVDA BUY, 'buy a lot') — 28x trailing profit vs 52x five-year average, 0.35 PEG, 66% operating margins; the $18B lease co-sign guarantee is the signal the world is watching. Bottom line: dollar-cost average; if the $1.7T signed-order backlog starts shrinking, all buy signals are off.
